turns.t: Hello, doctor. Oh dear, I've got this double vision, since yesterday, and it's the oddest thing. I see two of everything, when I look to the left.
When exactly did it start?
Yesterday afternoon, about three. I was watching the telly, and I thought there were two screens.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
All the time, if I look left. If I close one eye, it vanishes.
Any pain behind the eye, headache, or drooping of the eyelid?
No pain, no droop. Just the double vision.
You had your cataract surgery recently, didn't you?
Yes, the right eye, six weeks ago. They said it went very well.
Right. What are you taking at the moment?
Drops in the eye, still, one drop, three times a day. And my blood pressure tablet, I can't remember the name, it's a small white one.
Let me check, I've got it here. Amlodipine, 5 mg once a day. That one?
That's the one.
And your medical history?
High blood pressure. And I get migraines.
Do you live alone?
With my husband. He's at the bus stop, he'll be along.
Let me take your pulse and pressure. ~
Go on. ~
Pulse 76, blood pressure 156 over 94, temperature 36.7.
Is that high? ~
It's higher than I'd like. Let me check your eye movements. Follow my finger with your eyes.
Like that? ~
You can't move your right eye outwards fully, it stops short on looking to the right, and your pupils are equal and react normally.
Is that why it's double? ~
Yes, one of the muscles that moves the eye isn't working properly, and the two eyes aren't lining up. ~
What causes it? ~

It can be due to a nerve problem, sometimes related to high blood pressure or diabetes, and sometimes something more serious. I can't rule out a nerve palsy caused by a vascular problem, but I need tests.
Is it from the operation? ~
Unlikely, it's the eye muscles, not the lens. ~
Right. ~
Because it's sudden, I want to be sure, so I'd like you to go to the eye clinic today for a full assessment. ~
Today? Oh. ~
Yes. I'll ring ahead. And I'd like to take your blood pressure again after ten minutes.
Fine. ~
Don't drive, and if you get a drooping eyelid, a severe headache, or weakness in your face or limbs, call 999.
I will. ~
I'd like to see you again in three days.
Three days. Thank you, doctor. ~
